newsitem.title: DUBAI: Over 10 detained in Filipino murder case in Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Over 10 detained in Filipino murder case in Saudi.

text.p: More than 10 people were detained in connection with the murder of a Filipino designer in Saudi Arabia and several remain in police custody, a top Philippines diplomat said on Thursday.

Police found the body of 42-year-old Amoran Macausor, a Filipino Moslem who had lived in the kingdom for about 14 years, stabbed to death in his flat in the eastern Saudi city of al-Khobar on Saturday.
"More than 10 people were rounded up by the police and some were later released," said Muhammad Ali Basir Lucman, the Philippines' ambassador to Oman who is also the victims uncle.

"They are keeping some who made conflicting statements or where the authorities felt they were not telling the truth," Lucman told Reuters after he returned from visiting the scene of the crime in al-Khobar.
Macausor, a leading member of al-Khobar's Filipino community, owned a men's garment store together with a Saudi partner.
Members of Macausor's immediate family were expected to arrive in Saudi Arabia later on Thursday, assuming all travel documents were in order, the ambassador said.
Lucman said he hoped to receive more information from the Saudi authorities in one to two weeks.
"Of course I have full confidence in the Saudi authorities to deal with the case," he added.
About half a million Filipinos live and work in Saudi Arabia. Some four million Filipinos work overseas -- about a million of them in the Gulf -- in hopes of earning more than they can at home.
